slot.brief: Two-factory / urn partition problem: given total probabilities of a defect, use Bayes' theorem to find the posterior probability of the source; ask for the exact posterior value at level 4 difficulty.

stem: Factories $A$ and $B$ produce all items. If $P(D\mid A)=\dfrac16$, $P(D\mid B)=\dfrac14$ and the total probability of a defect $D$ is $\dfrac15$, find $P(B\mid D)$.

verdicts.working: Let $p=P(B)$. Then $\frac15=\frac{1-p}{6}+\frac p4$, giving $p=\frac25$. Thus $P(B\mid D)=\frac{(1/4)(2/5)}{1/5}=\frac12$.

working:
Let $p=P(A)$. Then $\dfrac{p}{6}+\dfrac{1-p}{4}=\dfrac15\Rightarrow p=\dfrac35$.
$P(B\mid D)=\dfrac{(\frac25)(\frac14)}{\frac15}=\dfrac12$.

Independent check: Let $p=P(B)$. Then $\frac15=\frac{1-p}{6}+\frac p4$, giving $p=\frac25$. Thus $P(B\mid D)=\frac{(1/4)(2/5)}{1/5}=\frac12$.
solution:
By Bayes’ theorem, first find $P(B)$. Let $P(B)=p$; then
$$\frac{1}{5}=\frac{1-p}{6}+\frac{p}{4}\quad\Rightarrow\quad p=\frac{2}{5}.$$
Hence $P(B\mid D)=\dfrac{P(D\mid B)P(B)}{P(D)}=\dfrac{(1/4)(2/5)}{1/5}=\dfrac{1}{2}.$
